items: Track Screen Time: Track exactly how much screen time your child actually gets for three full days before making any changes to your current setup.
Log Each Session: Record what device was used, what content was watched or played, how long it lasted, time of day, your child's mood, and what triggered the end of each session.
Identify Patterns: Look for specific times when tantrums occur, sessions that exceed 90 minutes, and mood changes that consistently happen before and after screen time.
Set a Realistic Baseline: Establish a "good enough" goal for your family rather than aiming for zero screen time, which is neither achievable nor necessary for most families.
Use 5-2-1 Verbal Warnings: Give your child explicit notice at 5 minutes, 2 minutes, and 1 minute before screen time ends so they can mentally prepare for the transition.
Set Up Visual Timers: Install a physical Time Timer, phone alarm, or smart display timer so your child has a concrete, hard-to-ignore signal that time is ending.
Offer a Last Thing Choice: Give your child a small sense of control by letting them choose to stop after one more episode or after finishing a game level.
Prepare a Post-Screen Activity: Have a specific engaging activity ready before ending screen time so your child has something concrete to transition to rather than facing an empty void.
Stay Emotionally Regulated: Keep your composure when your child protests or tantrums because your emotional regulation directly teaches your child how to handle disappointment.
Validate Their Feelings: Acknowledge that it is hard to stop something fun without blaming or shaming them for having emotions, which helps prevent escalation.
Follow Through Every Time: Consistently enforce every warning and timer without exception because your reliability teaches your child to trust the system over time.
Accept Normal Resistance: Understand that occasional resistance is a natural part of the process and does not mean the system is broken—consistency matters more than perfection.
